**💡 Today's learning:** "No added sugar juice is a healthy drink"

- **🤔 What people believe:** A pack that says "100% juice, no added sugar" must be light on sugar and as good as eating fruit.
- **🔬 The fact:** The label only says nothing extra was added. Cleveland Clinic notes one glass of orange juice has about 23 g of sugar, close to the American Heart Association's daily limit of 25 g for women, and nearly as much as a sugary soda. Juicing also strips out most of the fibre that keeps you full.
- **🎯 How they fool you:** The claim is true but answers the wrong question: it tells you what wasn't added, not how much sugar is inside. A glass squeezes 5 or 6 oranges' sugar into a few gulps. Check grams of sugar on the label, and eat the fruit instead.
- **Source:** https://health.clevelandclinic.org/is-100-percent-fruit-juice-as-healthy-as-it-sounds/
